data.turoyo: Komər mədle l dəsmale kumto, komər mkanfele qarʕe w nafəqle lu ḥarb.
data.translation: Er nahm ein schwarzes Tuch, wickelte es sich um den Kopf und ging hinaus zum Kampf.

rationale: Thin I Preterit cell; explicit head patient and preceding black-cloth covering, self-contained physical wrapping.

summary: Restore the final syllable of malwašlele
rationale: The supplied corpus of 60/319 reads “W malwašlele aǧ ǧulayḏe”. The entry has malwašle, omitting the final le syllable. Restoring that syllable is distinct from changing clitic boundaries.

summary: Restore ein in hüllte ihn ein
rationale: The separable verb einhüllen has lost its final ein. The source translation reads “hüllte ihn ein”, and the stem gloss is “einhüllen, einwickeln”.

summary: Preserve I mkanfele/mkanfəl exactly as the glossary labels it, despite the four-consonant root. Initial m- alone is not evidence for II or a new Q stem.
The clear active uses wrap a person (60/319) or a head (99/50). Detransitive Part. Pass. mkanfalto in 2/19 denotes a covered state, with b kurk naming the covering and no expressed agent.
JTM 2.1/2 securely supplies an Infectum-wa form but an uncertain technical meaning. No new published box/example is based on an unresolved sense; the form is recorded here for later confirmation.

Lookup knf confirms related wrapping meaning and a head-wrapping example. Its head note refers to 2/19; this is not proof that a second independent knf finite example of the same verse exists. Keep the roots separate pending editorial review.
In JTM 2.1/2, does mkanfəliwole fold a sheet, wrap a filling, gather layers, or stack them? Confirm the operation before publishing a culinary subsense and example.
How should knf and knfl be cross-referenced, including the knf head note citing 2/19? The exact mkanfəl family remains here.
